title: Proper diagonal of a finite-flat groupoid quotient
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], and stacks, representability and 2-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable morphism properties are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Flatness, local finite presentation, etaleness and properness use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A stack morphism is separated if its relative diagonal is proper. The inertia stack $I_{\mathcal A}$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows given by conjugating isomorphisms. Its projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The set $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the atlas topology [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. A scheme groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ has the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Its quotient $[U/R]$ is the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $T$-points, using [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Finite locally free means finite, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid of affine $k$-schemes with $s,t$ finite locally free. The algebraic stack $[U/R]$ has proper diagonal over $k$, and hence is separated over $k$. This assertion permits nonreduced stabilizer group schemes, variable ranks and empty schemes.

source.place: Tag 0DTY (lemma-properties-diagonal-from-presentation), part (6): proper source and target and separated U imply a separated quotient. Finite maps are proper by morphisms.tex Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); affine U is separated.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\mathcal Q=[U/R]$. Regard the schemes as their representable algebraic spaces. By the definition of finite locally free, $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply the flat-groupoid quotient theorem over $S$: $\mathcal Q$ is algebraic, $\Delta_{\mathcal Q/S}$ and $p:U\to\mathcal Q$ are representable by algebraic spaces, $p$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and $U\times_{\mathcal Q}U\simeq R$ with its source and target projections.

Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $U\times_kU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_k A)$ and $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_kU$ with the ring map $a\otimes a^{\prime}\mapsto s^*(a)t^*(a^{\prime})$. Since $s$ is finite, choose finite $A$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ via $s^*$. Each $b\in B$ is $\sum_i s^*(a_i)b_i=\sum_i j^*(a_i\otimes1)b_i$. Thus these same elements generate $B$ over $A\otimes_kA$. The affine definition of finite morphism now gives that $j$ is finite. This calculation works also for the zero ring and does not require constant rank or reducedness.

source.place: Tag 0DTY (lemma-properties-diagonal-from-presentation), condition (6) implies (5), specialized to affine schemes; schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); morphisms.tex Tag 01WH (definition-integral).

proof.text: The finite scheme morphism $j$ is proper by the finite-implies-proper lemma.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), finite implies affine and proper.

proof.text: The product $\mathcal Q\times_S\mathcal Q$ is algebraic by existence of algebraic-stack fibre products. Factor $q=p\times p:U\times_SU\to\mathcal Q\times_S\mathcal Q$ through $U\times_S\mathcal Q$. The first factor is the base change of $p$ along $U\times_S\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q$ (second projection), and the second factor is its base change along $\mathcal Q\times_S\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q$ (first projection). Base-change and composition calculus therefore make $q$ representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Its source is a scheme by the affine fibre-product formula.

source.place: Tag 0DTY (lemma-properties-diagonal-from-presentation), first paragraph of proof; algebraic.tex Tag 04T2 (lemma-2-fibre-product); stacks-properties.tex Section 04XB.

proof.text: The pullback of $\Delta_{\mathcal Q/S}$ along $q$ is $U\times_{\mathcal Q}U\to U\times_SU$, hence is $j$ under Step 1. Explicitly its objects consist of $(u_1,u_2)$ and an isomorphism $p(u_1)\simeq p(u_2)$: the extra diagonal object and its two isomorphisms can be eliminated by composing one with the inverse of the other. This is precisely the defining $2$-fibre product $U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$, and the identification preserves the two projections. Apply the representable proper fppf target test to $f=\Delta_{\mathcal Q/S}$ and $W=U\times_SU$: the target is algebraic by Step 4, the covering has all required properties by Step 4, and its pullback is proper by Step 3. Consequently $\Delta_{\mathcal Q/S}$ is proper, which is separatedness of $\mathcal Q$ over $k$ by the convention in the statement.
